previous_statement: Fix n and suppose D=sum_j A_j tensor B_j is a diagonal with sum_j||A_j||||B_j||=1. Put a_j=I_n tensor A_j, b_j=I_n tensor B_j, g_n(X,Y)=v_n(XY)-v_n(X)v_n(Y), w_prime_(D,n)(X)=sum_j v_n(a_j)g_n(b_j,X), and F_z(X,Y)=v_n(X)z(Y)-z(XY)+z(X)v_n(Y). These are local hypotheses and definitions; no existence of D and no identification w_prime_(D,n)=I_n tensor w_prime is asserted here. Direct expansion gives v_n(X)g_n(Y,Z)-g_n(XY,Z)+g_n(X,YZ)-g_n(X,Y)v_n(Z)=(v_n(X)v_n(Y))v_n(Z)-v_n(X)(v_n(Y)v_n(Z)); since ||v_n(T)||<=(1+d)||T||, the epsilon-associativity bound makes the residual at most epsilon(1+d)^3||X||||Y||||Z||<=2epsilon||X||||Y||||Z|| when d+epsilon<=1/4. Expand F_(w_prime_(D,n)). First reassociate v_n(X)(v_n(a_j)g_n(b_j,Y)) and replace v_n(X)v_n(a_j) by v_n(Xa_j). Entrywise amplification of XD=DX then changes sum_j v_n(Xa_j)g_n(b_j,Y) exactly into sum_j v_n(a_j)g_n(b_jX,Y). Reassociate the third term to put v_n(a_j) outside, and apply the displayed cocycle identity to (b_j,X,Y), obtaining sum_j v_n(a_j)(v_n(b_j)g_n(X,Y)) up to its residual. Reassociate this expression, replace v_n(a_j)v_n(b_j) by v_n(a_jb_j), and use sum_j a_jb_j=I_n tensor pi(D)=I. Finally replace v_n(I)g_n(X,Y) by g_n(X,Y). After summing in j, the respective errors are bounded by epsilon(1+d)^2 d, (1+epsilon)d^2, epsilon(1+d)^2 d, 2(1+epsilon)(1+d)epsilon, epsilon(1+d)^2 d, (1+epsilon)d^2, and ((1+epsilon)d+epsilon)d, all multiplied by ||X||||Y|| sum_j||A_j||||B_j||. For d+epsilon<=1/4 their sum is at most 100(d^2+epsilon)||X||||Y||. Hence ||F_(w_prime_(D,n))(X,Y)-g_n(X,Y)||<=100(d^2+epsilon)||X||||Y|| uniformly in n and in every normalized diagonal satisfying the stated local hypothesis.
new_statement: Fix n. The following inequalities are not extra hypotheses: def-extended-epsilon-cstar-algebra says M_n tensor A is an epsilon-C*-algebra, and registered def-epsilon-cstar-algebra therefore gives ||ST||<=(1+epsilon)||S||||T||, ||(ST)R-S(TR)||<=epsilon||S||||T||||R||, the isometric anti-multiplicative involution, and the epsilon-unit bounds. Likewise, def-extended-delta-inclusion says v_n=I_n tensor v is a d-inclusion; unpacking its d-homomorphism and two-sided norm clauses gives ||v_n(T)||<=(1+d)||T||, ||v_n(ST)-v_n(S)v_n(T)||<=d||S||||T||, ||v_n(I)-I||<=d, and dagger preservation. By the registered external GT-kitaev-standard-diagonal choose D=sum_j A_j tensor B_j with sum_j||A_j||||B_j||=1, XD=DX, and sum_j A_jB_j=I. Put a_j=I_n tensor A_j, b_j=I_n tensor B_j, g_n(X,Y)=v_n(XY)-v_n(X)v_n(Y), w_prime_n(X)=sum_j v_n(a_j)g_n(b_j,X), and F_z(X,Y)=v_n(X)z(Y)-z(XY)+z(X)v_n(Y). Direct expansion, using associativity in the source algebra B, gives v_n(X)g_n(Y,Z)-g_n(XY,Z)+g_n(X,YZ)-g_n(X,Y)v_n(Z)=(v_n(X)v_n(Y))v_n(Z)-v_n(X)(v_n(Y)v_n(Z)); the registered epsilon-associativity inequality bounds the right side by epsilon(1+d)^3||X||||Y||||Z||<=2epsilon||X||||Y||||Z|| when d+epsilon<=1/4. Expand F_(w_prime_n). Reassociate v_n(X)(v_n(a_j)g_n(b_j,Y)), replace v_n(X)v_n(a_j) by v_n(Xa_j), and use the amplified identity XD=DX to change the summed expression exactly to sum_j v_n(a_j)g_n(b_jX,Y). Reassociate the third term to put v_n(a_j) outside and apply the displayed cocycle identity to (b_j,X,Y), giving sum_j v_n(a_j)(v_n(b_j)g_n(X,Y)) up to its residual. Reassociate again, replace v_n(a_j)v_n(b_j) by v_n(a_jb_j), use sum_j a_jb_j=I, and finally replace v_n(I)g_n(X,Y) by g_n(X,Y). The seven errors, in this order, are bounded by epsilon(1+d)^2*d, (1+epsilon)d^2, epsilon(1+d)^2*d, 2(1+epsilon)(1+d)epsilon, epsilon(1+d)^2*d, (1+epsilon)d^2, and ((1+epsilon)d+epsilon)d, times ||X||||Y|| sum_j||A_j||||B_j||. Each bound follows respectively from the explicitly cited epsilon-associativity, d-multiplicativity, product, and epsilon-unit/d-unit inequalities. Since the weight sum is 1 and d+epsilon<=1/4, their sum is at most 100(d^2+epsilon)||X||||Y||. Hence ||F_(w_prime_n)(X,Y)-g_n(X,Y)||<=100(d^2+epsilon)||X||||Y|| uniformly in n.
